name: Asian Ginseng
summary: Asian ginseng (Panax ginseng) is a slow-growing root whose ginsenosides are its characteristic compounds; it is a classic adaptogen taken for energy, cognition, and blood sugar. For glucose, a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials across the Panax genus found that ginseng modestly lowered fasting blood glucose compared with control, although the effect was small and the trials were varied and often short. Evidence for its other traditional uses, such as memory and fatigue, is mixed. Ginseng may interact with blood thinners and with diabetes medications.
description: May modestly support memory outcomes, but evidence is mixed for broader cognition. Caveat: Do not imply broad attention/executive-function benefit or stimulation without safety context.
safetyNotes: Generally well tolerated for most users.

sources.title: Effects of Ginseng on Cognitive Function: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
sources.citation: 15 RCTs/671 participants; memory effect signal; no positive effect on overall cognition, attention, executive function.

claimMap.claim: Ginseng may have a small memory-support signal, but not enough to claim broad cognition, attention, or executive-function benefits.
